title: fix(perf): hand closed-loop warmup over without draining the server
body:
## Summary

Closed-loop runs report a `p99` TTFT that is several times the server's real steady-state `p99`, because the start-up burst lands inside the measured window. Enabling `--warmup-num` did not help. This PR hands the concurrency slots from warmup over to the measured requests without draining them in between, which puts the reported percentiles on the steady-state values.

Fixes #1627

### Relation to #1547

#1547 (`startup_ramp_seconds`) targets the same underlying phenomenon -- a cohort of requests released simultaneously at the start of a phase -- but on the multi-turn path, and it addresses it by staggering the release itself. This PR does not touch multi-turn and does not supersede that discussion; it shows that on the single-turn closed-loop path the burst can be absorbed by the warmup requests that are already being sent, with no new CLI surface and no under-loaded stretch inside the measured window. Whether the same reasoning should replace the ramp for multi-turn is left to #1547.

## Root cause

A closed-loop run at concurrency `N` measures a closed queueing network with `N` circulating jobs. The quantity of interest is the stationary TTFT distribution at occupancy `N`, where the `N` in-flight requests are spread across phases — a few prefilling, most decoding.

The dispatcher started from the worst possible initial condition. `_run_phase` ended with a barrier (`await asyncio.gather(*in_flight)`), so warmup drained server occupancy back to zero, and the measured phase then released its first `N` requests within the same event-loop tick. All `N` were in the prefill phase simultaneously, so each queued behind the others' prefill:

* prefill queue depth at the start: `N`
* prefill queue depth in steady state: `N × (prefill time / whole request time)`, normally well below one

TTFT is the metric most sensitive to that difference. The collected samples are therefore a **mixture** of `N` start-up samples and `number − N` steady-state samples, while `calculate_percentiles` treats them as a single distribution. Once `N / number` exceeds 1%, `p99` is determined by the start-up samples alone.

Warmup could not fix this on its own: because of the barrier, occupancy returned to zero and the measured window re-created the same synchronised burst.

## What changed

* `ClosedLoopStrategy` dispatches warmup and measured requests through **one loop and one semaphore**, with no barrier between them. Each warmup completion releases exactly one measured request into a server that already holds `parallel - 1` requests mid-flight, so the measured portion inherits a steady-state arrival pattern from its first sample onwards.
* `BenchmarkStrategy._collect_requests()` keeps the `(request, is_warmup)` stream in order; `_partition_requests` is untouched and still used by open-loop.
* The `--duration` deadline is armed when the **first measured request is actually sent**, i.e. once it holds a concurrency slot, so warmup does not consume the timed budget. Arming on task creation would not work: creation is bounded by `max_in_flight` rather than by the semaphore, so measured tasks are queued while warmup still holds every slot and the clock would start at ~t0. With the send-based anchor the measured window begins exactly where measurement begins.
* `metrics_consumer` closes the warmup progress bar on completion count instead of on the first measured item, because warmup and measured results now interleave briefly around the hand-over.
* `run_benchmark` warns when warmup cannot cover every concurrency slot, and names the value that would.

Only the closed-loop single-turn path is touched. Open-loop and multi-turn dispatch are unchanged.

## Verification on a real endpoint

Qwen2.5-0.5B on vLLM, `--parallel 32 --number 320`, ~4k-token prompts, `--max-tokens 64`.

*Contaminated* = measured requests in the opening cohort whose TTFT exceeds the steady-state (tail) `p99`. It is used instead of a head/tail ratio because the server's baseline latency drifts between runs, while this count is normalised per run.

| `--warmup-num` | opening cohort dispatched over | contaminated | reported p99 | steady-state p99 | overstated | reported max | steady-state max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 9 ms | 32 / 32 | 1609 ms | 384 ms | 4.19x | 1724 ms | 457 ms |
| 8 | 1555 ms | 25 / 32 | 1362 ms | 546 ms | 2.50x | 1476 ms | 556 ms |
| 32 (= `--parallel`) | 934 ms | 0 / 32 | 321 ms | 321 ms | 1.00x | 355 ms | 355 ms |
| 64 (= 2x `--parallel`) | 1207 ms | 0 / 32 | 410 ms | 416 ms | 0.99x | 430 ms | 430 ms |

Readings:

* At `--warmup-num >= --parallel` the reported `p99` equals the steady-state `p99` exactly, and so does `max`.
* The dispatch span of the opening cohort is the direct signature of the hand-over: 9 ms when every request is released at once, ~1 s once warmup releases them one at a time.
* The warning is quantitatively accurate. At `--warmup-num 8` it states that 24 measured requests are released at once alongside the warmup ones; the measured contamination is 25 of 32, i.e. the arithmetic in the warning matches reality to within one sample.
* For reference, the previous code with `--warmup-num 32` still reported `p99` 2178 ms against a steady-state 818 ms, confirming that warmup alone could not remove the burst before this change.

A residual single outlier in the `max` column at `--warmup-num == --parallel` was observed in some runs and not in others. The cause was not investigated -- one hypothesis is two warmup completions coinciding and releasing two measured requests at once -- so it is not documented as a mechanism; the docs only suggest a larger value when the `max` column matters.

### One case this does not fix: a fixed output length

`--min-tokens == --max-tokens` (plus `ignore_eos`) is the usual way to make a run reproducible, but it also removes all service-time variance, so a cohort that starts together finishes together and is re-released together. That synchronised state is a fixed point of the closed loop, so the burst repeats every cycle instead of decaying: neither warmup nor a larger `--number` helps, and the symptom is a TTFT ramp with a period of `--parallel`.

Measured on the same endpoint (`parallel=8 number=96 prompt=2000`), using the **second half** of each run so a decaying transient cannot be mistaken for the effect. Mean TTFT by within-cycle position:

| config | out tokens | mean TTFT by position (ms) | ramp |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| fixed 64 + `ignore_eos` | all 64 | 41 52 50 40 53 65 68 75 | **1.86x** |
| `--max-tokens 48 64` | 17 distinct, 48-64 | 49 49 60 60 64 54 44 49 | 1.00x |
| `--open-loop --rate 4`, fixed 64 | all 64 | 34 31 32 32 33 31 32 33 | 1.00x |

The lock needs both zero variance **and** the closed-loop feedback, so breaking either removes it. No code change is warranted -- a deterministic closed network genuinely has the synchronised state as its steady state, and both remedies already exist. This PR only documents it under `--min-tokens`, which is where users configure it. (`--min-tokens` alone cannot restore variance: `ignore_eos` plus a fixed `--max-tokens` pins the length regardless of the floor.)

## Behaviour changes

**`--warmup-num` no longer drains before the measured window.** Warmup requests are still excluded from every metric, but they now overlap the start of the measured portion instead of finishing in isolation. Users who already pass `--warmup-num` will see their reported `p99` drop, because it stops including the start-up burst. Runs without warmup are unaffected.

**A value below `--parallel` degrades gracefully.** It leaves part of the burst inside the measured window; the run warns and names the value that would cover every slot (`--parallel`, or `2 x --parallel` when the `max` column also matters). No auto-adjustment of the value is introduced.

**`--rate` pacing now spans the whole stream.** Inter-arrival targets are computed once over `warmup + number` requests (`total / rate`) rather than per phase. The total target time is unchanged and the existing "behind schedule dispatches immediately" handling still applies, but the measured requests' absolute targets are no longer re-anchored after warmup has drained. This makes `--rate` a single global request rate.

## Tests

`tests/perf/test_closed_loop_warmup_handoff.py` (12 cases), driven with a fake client that records server occupancy at each dispatch, plus one end-to-end case through `run_benchmark` against a mock OpenAI server:

* the first measured request dispatches while `parallel - 1` requests are still in flight, and occupancy never returns to zero mid-stream
* dispatch order, occupancy cap, and graceful degradation when warmup covers only part of the slots
* `--duration` armed on the first measured send: warmup is exempt from the cap, and the anchor is asserted to fall no earlier than the first freed slot (a `duration=0` case cannot distinguish the two anchors)
* warning text for warmup disabled / partially covering, and silence when it covers every slot
* end to end: warmup requests reach the server and stay out of the result database

Scope note: cases covering code this PR does not change were deliberately left out -- `Arguments.warmup_count` is untouched here, the semaphore cap is pre-existing, and failure/cancellation for `ClosedLoopStrategy` is already parametrized in `test_async_lifecycle.py::test_strategy_failure_cancels_in_flight_requests`.

Regressions: `pytest tests/perf` (excluding the cases that need a live endpoint) and `tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite` pass; `pre-commit` is clean.

title: fix(perf): abort request generation when a plugin returns None for the whole dataset
body:
Follow-up to #1571 (issue #1565). That PR fixed the swallow-to-`None` path in `OpenaiPlugin`, but left one residual hang untouched, as noted in the #1565 discussion.

## Problem

`get_requests()._generate_from_dataset()` cycles the dataset and only advances `count` when `build_request()` returns a request:

```python
while count < total_count:
    request = api_plugin.build_request(dataset_messages[dataset_index])
    if request is not None:
        yield request, count < warmup_count
        count += 1
    dataset_index = (dataset_index + 1) % num_messages
```

If a plugin returns `None` for **every** message, `count` never advances and the loop has no `await` — it starves the event loop forever. The other four API plugins (embedding / rerank / custom / dashscope) still legitimately return `None` for unusable/empty input, so this is reachable.

## Fix

Guard the loop with a full-pass invariant: if a whole cycle over the dataset yields no request, raise with the plugin name instead of spinning.

```python
consecutive_skips += 1
if consecutive_skips >= num_messages:
    raise ValueError(f'{type(api_plugin).__name__}.build_request() returned None for every one of the {num_messages} dataset message(s); no request could be generated.')
```

## Verification

New test `test_all_none_requests_abort_instead_of_hanging`:
- **without** the guard it hangs (`pytest-timeout` fires at `benchmark.py:95`),
- **with** the guard it raises `ValueError` fast.

`tests/perf/test_request_generation.py`: 14 passed. `make lint` clean.

title: fix(web): render local-path media in both dashboard chains
body: ## What Removes the legacy Gradio-era image convention from `messages_to_markdown` and makes the Web dashboard resolve server-side media paths in **both** rendering chains. ## Why `messages_to_markdown` emitted `![image](gradio_api/file=)`, introduced by #1019 when the dashboard was Gradio-based. That convention is dead: - `gradio` appears in no `requirements/*.txt` and not in `pyproject.toml` - `evalscope app` is only a `[DEPRECATED] Use "evalscope service" instead` alias - nothing in Python code, `evalscope/web/src` or `tests/` interprets `gradio_api` - the React dashboard serves server-side files via `/api/v1/reports/media/file?path=` Consequence: every benchmark that puts a local path in `ContentImage` (miniwob, browsergym, general_vqa custom data, …) had broken images in the compare view, and `Sample.pretty_print` printed the unusable prefix as noise. Dropping the prefix alone is not enough — `MarkdownRenderer` passed the markdown `src` straight to `ImageLightbox`, which renders `` verbatim. Only the structured `Messages` chain proxied media, via the module-private `resolveMediaSrc` in `MediaBlocks.tsx`. ## Changes 1. **`evalscope/api/messages/chat_message.py`** — emit `![image]({abs_path})` instead of the `gradio_api/file=` form. 2. **`evalscope/web/src/utils/media.ts`** (new) — `resolveMediaSrc` extracted here and shared. It is *not* exported from `MediaBlocks.tsx` because `MediaBlocks` already imports `MarkdownRenderer`, so re-importing would create a cycle. 3. **`MarkdownRenderer.tsx`** — the `img` renderer now resolves `src` through `resolveMediaSrc`, so the markdown chain proxies local paths exactly like the structured chain. 4. **`evalscope/utils/data_utils.py`** — absolutise local media paths when serialising prediction messages (see below). ### Extra fix: relative paths in the structured chain While verifying, the single-report detail view turned out to be broken too — not by this change, but pre-existing on `main`. `ContentImage` values may be **relative** paths (the custom VQA data behind `general_vqa` uses `custom_eval/multimodal/images/dog.jpg`). Note this resolution is relative to the **service process CWD** — that constraint already applied to the markdown chain (`messages_markdown` is computed at read time), so it is not newly introduced. ## Verification Real run: `general_vqa` on the custom VQA sample data, DashScope `qwen-vl-plus` + `qwen-vl-max`, then a live dashboard. ## #1546 — GPQA-Diamond misjudged when the model leaves its reasoning in the output

**Two independent causes.**

1. `parse_answers` allowed its capture group to match whitespace only. When a model restated the required format (`ANSWER: [LETTER]`) before answering, that echo matched first with an empty capture and the real answer was discarded. The line-anchored pattern also misses an answer that directly follows an unpaired `</think>` tag. The capture group now has to start with an alphanumeric character.

2. More importantly, **configured filters never reached multi-choice extraction.** `filter_prediction()` runs the filter ensemble and passes the filtered text into `extract_answer(prediction, task_state)`, but `MultiChoiceAdapter.extract_answer` (and the mmmu / a_okvqa / ai2d / cmmu / agieval adapters) dropped the `prediction` argument and let `parse_answers` re-read `task_state.output.completion`. A user who set `filters={'remove_until': '</think>'}` to strip a reasoning block still got the raw completion parsed, so there was no way to work around bad extraction. `parse_answers` / `parse_answers_zh` now accept an optional `completion` argument and those callers pass the filtered prediction.

This is not a regression: both mechanisms landed in the same v1.0 refactor (#739) and were never wired together. `parse_answers(state)` follows the upstream inspect_ai style where scorers read `TaskState` directly and no filter layer exists, while `filters` follows the lm-eval-harness style of operating on prediction strings. `extract_answer` is the seam where they should meet.

**Verification** — 20 gpqa_diamond + 40 iquiz samples (iquiz exercises the Chinese `parse_answers_zh` path), re-scored from identical cached predictions via `use_cache` + `rerun_review`:

| | gpqa | iquiz IQ | iquiz EQ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 0.75 | 1.0 | 0.75 |
| after | 0.75 | 1.0 | 0.75 |

60/60 samples identical per-sample (`extracted_prediction` and `value`), so default runs are unaffected. No benchmark ships default `filters`; they only ever come from user `dataset_args`.

Counter-check that filters are genuinely wired now — same cached predictions with a deliberately non-matching `regex` filter:

| | gpqa mean_acc |
| --- | --- |
| before | 0.75 (filter silently ignored) |
| after | 0.0 (filter respected) |

## #1543 — ifeval scores differ for identical responses

Pinning `DetectorFactory.seed` alone was not enough. `langdetect.detect()` builds its process-global detector factory lazily and **without a lock**, so concurrent first calls race and some threads detect against language profiles that are still half-loaded. That is exactly the shape of a real evaluation: cold start plus parallel review. The factory is now built once, under a lock, before any detection — ifeval does it on first use via double-checked locking, multi-if at import time while still single-threaded.

**Verification** — 128 checks over 16 threads against a cold factory, for one identical response:

| | result set |
| --- | --- |
| before any fix | `{False, True}` |
| seed pinned only | `{False, True}` |
| seed + locked warm-up | `{True}` |

The regression test reproduces the race by dropping the private global factory and fails on both earlier variants. `evalscope eval --datasets ifeval --limit 5 --repeats 3` is now consistent across repeats.

## #1542 — Tau-bench docs said pass@k while the default reports pass^k

`mean_and_pass_hat_k` computes `C(c, k) / C(n, k)`, the probability that *all* k attempts succeed, which is the `pass^k` metric defined by the tau-bench paper. The default aggregation is therefore correct and the wording was wrong. The descriptions of `tau_bench`, `tau2_bench` and `tau3_bench` now say `pass^k`, spell out the difference from `pass@k`, and point at `mean_and_pass_at_k` for users who want the latter. Benchmark pages and `_meta` caches were regenerated through the `benchmark-info` pipeline; the two hand-written `third_party/tau3_bench.md` pages were updated directly.

`tau3_bench` also could not be regenerated at all: its adapter resolved the dataset in `__init__`, which crashes with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'dataset_hub'` when the docs pipeline instantiates adapters without a task config. Dataset preparation is now skipped when there is no task config.

## #1541 — LiveCodeBench did not send the official system prompt

The system messages defined in `live_code_bench/prompts.py` were never used as a system message, so EvalScope sent only a user message while the official `lcb_runner` sends system + user. `SYSTEM_MESSAGE_GENERIC` is now registered as the benchmark system prompt.

**⚠️ Behaviour change:** LiveCodeBench scores are no longer directly comparable with earlier EvalScope runs. Users who need the previous behaviour can set `dataset_args={'live_code_bench': {'system_prompt': None}}`.

Verified on a real `release_v1` run that the request really carries `role=system` followed by `role=user`, and that evaluation still completes (8/8 on those samples, with and without the system prompt — too small a sample to quantify the score delta reported in the issue).

---

## Deliberately not in this PR

- **Unpaired `</think>` is still not stripped automatically.** `parse_content_with_reasoning` only handles paired tags, while thinking models prefill `<think>` via their chat template and emit only the closing tag. Rather than changing what every benchmark records as `prediction`, the FAQ now documents that limit and recommends enabling a reasoning parser on the inference engine, configuring `remove_until`, or using `judge_strategy=llm_recall`. Also corrected: the FAQ previously claimed `<think>...</think>` is handled automatically without qualification.
- **`_fallback_parse_answer` remains unconstrained.** It scans the whole text for the last uppercase letter and returns it without validating against the available choices, so `ANSWER: [B] because XYZ` still yields `Z`. Left for a follow-up because tightening it lowers scores for samples that currently pass by accident.

## Test plan

- `make lint` — all hooks pass.
- New `tests/test_multi_choices.py` (8 tests): answer-shape coverage, the `completion` override for both language paths, and a regression test asserting that a configured filter reaches extraction (fails on the previous code).
- New `tests/benchmark/test_ifeval_language_checkers.py` (2 tests): determinism under concurrency against a cold factory, and the pinned seed.
- New `tests/benchmark/test_live_code_bench_prompt.py` (2 tests): the registered system prompt and the resulting system + user message pair.
- `pytest tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite` passes; `tests/api/test_default_data_adapter.py` (existing system-prompt coverage) still passes.
- Live API runs: `ifeval --repeats 3`, `gpqa_diamond` with and without filters, `live_code_bench release_v1`.
- Sphinx builds for `docs/en` and `docs/zh` succeed (the one remaining warning is a pre-existing broken xref in `benchmarks/miniwob.md`).

title: fix(evaluator): log resolved sample total and warn on per-subset --limit
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1496.

`--limit` is applied **per subset**, so on multi-subset datasets the run size is silently multiplied. For example `mmlu_redux --limit 300` (57 subsets × 100 items) is a no-op and runs 5700 items/model — the user in #1496 only caught it from item-count telemetry mid-run, after a ~2h plan had already become ~65h.

The total *is* present in the tqdm bar's denominator, but that only appears once the pool starts, is easy to skim past as a progress denominator, and doesn't render as a bar under non-TTY/redirected output (the common case for long evals).

## Changes

- **Log the resolved sample total up front**, right after loading and before any work starts:
  - `mmlu: 849 samples to evaluate (3 subsets)` (INFO, no limit)
  - `mmlu: 12 samples to evaluate (3 subsets, --limit=4 per subset). Remove `--limit` for a formal evaluation.` (**WARNING** when `--limit` is set)
- The total is computed from the already-limited `dataset_dict`, so it is always accurate (including the no-op case where `limit` exceeds a subset's size).
- **Log-flow cleanup** in `DefaultEvaluator.eval()`:
  - Drop the internal `Unified pool` jargon.
  - Only log the cache split when resuming (`total_cached > 0`); otherwise it just duplicated the total.
  - Replace the redundant second `... finished` line with a phase marker (`predictions complete, aggregating scores...`).

## Testing

Ran `mock_llm` on `mmlu` (multi-subset) verifying all branches:

```

# fresh, with limit -> WARNING
mmlu: 12 samples to evaluate (3 subsets, --limit=4 per subset). Remove `--limit` for a formal evaluation.
```

title: fix(config): reject unknown task-config keys and consolidate deprecation/serialization
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1619 and hardens the `TaskConfig` layer. Previously a misspelled or
hyphenated config key (e.g. `eval-batch-size` instead of `eval_batch_size`)
was silently dropped by Pydantic's default `extra='ignore'`, leaving the
value at its default with no feedback — the user in #1619 only noticed
because vLLM kept `running=1`.

## What changed

### Unknown-key rejection (#1619 root cause)
- `BaseArgument` now uses `extra='forbid'`. `from_dict` raises with a
  top-level **"did you mean"** suggestion (e.g. `'eval-batch-size' ->
  'eval_batch_size'`) while leaving nested Pydantic errors — which already
  report the full path — untouched.
- Verified against 24 real historical output snapshots: **zero net new
  failures** (the existing `judge_worker_num` removal error already covered
  the same input class).

### eval_batch_size default
- Defaults to **8** for remote API eval types (`openai_api`,
  `openai_responses_api`, `anthropic_api`, `litellm`); local/checkpoint stays
  `1`. CLI `--eval-batch-size` default is `None` so the dynamic default can
  apply, and an explicit value always wins.

### eval_type alias normalization
- Deprecated aliases are normalized at input (`checkpoint` -> `llm_ckpt`,
  `server` -> `openai_api`). This fixes two latent bugs: `checkpoint` was
  missing its default `model_args`, and `server` was missing the concurrent
  default — both because downstream `eval_type ==` checks compared against the
  canonical value only.
- Removes the unused `EvalType.SERVICE` constant; aligns the
  `server`/`checkpoint` model-API deprecation removal to `v2.0.0`.

### Internal cleanup (behavior-preserving)
- Deprecation handling is split by whether it needs the coerced field value:
  a `mode='before'` validator `_migrate_deprecated_input` does **pure key
  renames** (judge keys, eval_type alias) on the raw input, while
  `_apply_typed_config_deprecations` and `_init_default_sandbox_config` run
  **after validation** for anything that must read a coerced value
  (timeout/stream/n forwarding, sandbox legacy-field folding). Keeping the
  sandbox fold in the after-validator lets it read the already-coerced
  `use_sandbox` bool instead of re-implementing Pydantic's coercion.
- Unifies the two divergent serialization paths (`to_dict` for YAML,
  `_to_update_dict` for merge) into a single `_serialize(purpose)` core.
  `agent_config` is now set-only on both paths, so snapshots no longer pin
  default values (was full-dumped by `to_dict` before).

## Compatibility note

`extra='forbid'` is stricter than before. Snapshot round-trip and 24 real
historical configs were checked and behave identically; deprecated keys still
migrate. Any config carrying a truly unknown key will now error instead of
silently ignoring it — this is the intended fix.

## Testing
- New `tests/api/test_task_config_validation.py` (34 cases): unknown-key
  rejection + suggestion, nested-key attribution, alias normalization,
  remote-API default, sandbox legacy folding (incl. falsy string coercion),
  serialization round-trip, and `update()` merge semantics.
- `tests/api`: 274 passed (4 unrelated pre-existing failures).
- `make lint` clean; CI smoke `test_ci_lite` passes.

title: fix(agent): make AgentLoop own the nudge count and give models an honest reminder
body:
Follow-up to #1581 (merged). That PR fixed the one broken marker string in
`swe_bench_toolcall`; this one removes the mechanism that produced the bug, fixes
the same latent defect in `swe_bench_backticks`, and then removes two further
instances of the same pattern found along the way. Thanks @Roovelrz for the
diagnosis and the first fix.

## The pattern, not the instance

The original bug was one instance of *deriving state that another party owns*.
Strategies answered "how many nudges have I injected?" by substring-matching a
reminder in `ctx.messages`, while `AgentLoop` is the only party that injects it.
Any drift between the assumed marker and the injected text silently yields `0`,
which reads as "never nudged" and lets a stuck model nudge on **every** no-tool
turn up to `max_steps` (250 for SWE-bench). The failure mode of the counting
mechanism was exactly the bug it existed to prevent, and it failed silently.

Two of four strategies were broken this way: `swe_bench_toolcall` matched a
string the loop never writes (fixed in #1581); `swe_bench_backticks` matched a
`ParsedAction.error` the loop only records in the trace. `function_calling` /
`react` worked only by luck — their marker is a prefix of `NUDGE_PROMPT`.

## Changes

**1. Authoritative nudge count.** `AgentContext.nudge_count` is owned by
`AgentLoop`, read by a single default `should_nudge`. All four strategies drop
their hand-rolled implementations. Reading a typed field fails loud on
regression instead of silently degrading.

**2. Consecutive, not per-episode.** The counters reset on every tool-calling
turn, so a budget bounds a *consecutive* streak. Without this a single stray
text-only turn late in a long task ends the run early.

**3. Honest reminder text.** `AgentStrategy.nudge_message` returns
`parsed.error` when present, else a strategy-appropriate prompt. The generic
"call the submit tool" misleads for `swe_bench_*` (completion is a bash
sentinel) and for BrowserGym/MiniWoB (`include_submit_tool=False`).

**4. Explicit turn outcome.** `if not parsed.tool_calls` branched on a *symptom*
shared by two unrelated states: a malformed turn that tried to act, and an idle
turn that only produced text. `ParsedAction.outcome` (`TurnOutcome.ACT /
MALFORMED / IDLE`) names them and defines the precedence in one place.

**5. Separate budgets.** A malformed turn is told the exact rule it broke, so it
is strictly more recoverable than a model replying in prose — yet it used to get
the same or fewer retries. `max_parse_error_nudges = 3` /
`ctx.parse_error_nudge_count` are now independent of `max_nudges = 2` /
`ctx.nudge_count`; an ACT turn resets both.

**6. Distinct terminal source.** An exhausted malformed streak was reported as
`implicit_no_nudge` ("the model stopped calling tools") when the model was in
fact calling tools and only breaking the protocol. New
`SubmissionSources.PARSE_ERROR_EXHAUSTED`, and the SUBMIT payload now carries
`outcome` / `error` / `raw_text_preview` instead of a `final_answer` the loop
does not own.

**7. Two score-losing fixes found while validating.** A live SWE-bench run
surfaced these:
- `swe_bench_backticks.extract_final_answer` returned the *nudge reminder text*
  as the patch when a run ended on a nudge (nudges are `ChatMessageUser` too).
  Nudges are now identified from the trace's NUDGE events.
- Both SWE-bench adapters recovered a diff via
  `str(msg.content or '') or msg.text`. For any reasoning model `content` is a
  `list[Content]` whose `str()` is a non-empty Python repr, so `msg.text` was
  dead code and `extract_diff` passed the repr through to the grader — `git
  apply` then fails. Fixed at all four sites that stringified message content.

**8. Trace view surfaces it.** `NudgeRow` shows an idle/malformed badge and the
submit pill shows its source, so a reminder is attributable without reading
JSONL. Three i18n keys added earlier were dead — `trace.loopMessage.*` is only
consulted for `error`-type events — and are replaced by keys the renderers
actually ask for. `keyCoverage.test.ts` gains the reverse check that would have
caught them.

## Behavior changes

- `swe_bench_backticks`: unbounded nudge → at most 2 consecutive.
- `swe_bench_toolcall`: at most 1 **consecutive** (was 1 per episode). Its
  malformed path is unreachable — `parse_output` never sets `error`.
- Malformed retries: previously unbounded (the error text did not match the
  marker) → now 3 consecutive.
- Worst-case consecutive nudges rises from 2 to 5, when a model alternates
  malformed and idle turns and drains both budgets in one streak.
- `nudge_message` is now a **required** member of the strategy contract: the loop
  calls it unconditionally, so an implementation satisfying the Protocol
  structurally rather than by subclassing raises `AttributeError`.
- `TurnOutcome` is exported from `evalscope.api.agent`.
- No benchmark score changes: what gets submitted is untouched except where it
  was previously wrong (point 7).

## Validation

- `tests/agent` + `tests/api`: 334 passed / 8 skipped (was 308 on the base).
- Frontend: `tsc -b`, `eslint`, `drift:locale` clean; vitest 65 files / 491 tests.
- **Mutation-tested**: 17 injected defects each redden a specific guard —
  outcome precedence, collapsing the two counters, dropping either reset,
  reverting the terminal source, widening a budget, dropping the sentinel from a
  reminder, and each of the four `str(content)` sites.
- **Live E2E** (Docker + qwen3-max): `swe_bench_verified_agentic_backticks`
  (exercises the nudge path: 2 nudges then `implicit_no_nudge`), `gaia`
  (`react` + submit, 33.3%, no nudges — confirms the normal path is intact),
  `miniwob` (`function_calling` with `max_tool_calls_per_turn=1`).
- **Trace view verified in a browser** against the real SWE-bench run: both the
  nudge badges and `Submit · no tool call` render as intended.

## Rejected

`AgentTrace.final_prediction` was implemented and then reverted. The live run
showed it holding the repr of a content list where the reported prediction was
`''`: resolution is an adapter-level decision (the SWE-bench overrides layer
their own diff recovery), so the loop cannot own it, and the convergence point
exposed a separate pre-existing defect in assigning `''` to
`ModelOutput.completion` for list content. A field advertised as the single
source of truth while carrying a wrong value is worse than no field.

Refs #1577, #1581

title: fix(gpqa): seed choice shuffle from the question so rerun-review is reproducible
body:
## Problem

`--rerun-review` on `gpqa_diamond` reports ~25% accuracy (chance level for four
options) instead of reproducing the original score. Reported in #1579, with the
reporter correctly pointing at the shuffle in `gpqa_adapter.py`.

`_process_input` shuffled the four options through the unseeded global RNG, so
`record_to_sample` was not a pure function — the option order, and therefore the
target letter, changed on every dataset build:

```python
random.shuffle(choices)
correct_answer_index = choices.index(preprocess(input_d['Correct Answer']))
```

On a rerun the dataset is rebuilt from scratch while predictions are restored
from the cache. `ModelResult.to_task_state` looks the sample up as
`dataset[self.index]`, so the cached completion — produced under the *original*
option order — is scored against an answer key derived from a *new* shuffle.
The reporter's example (`target: "A"` on the first run, `target: "C"` on the
rerun, same question and same prompt) is exactly this.

## Change

Derive the shuffle order from `sha256(question)`, so `_process_input` becomes a
pure function:

- same question always produces the same option order and target letter;
- different questions still get different orders, so the position-bias
  protection the shuffle exists for is preserved;
- the result no longer depends on global RNG state (dataset shuffling, other
  adapters, model sampling).

`gpqa_diamond` was the only adapter shuffling choices this way — everything
else goes through the framework-level `shuffle_choices` path, which already
accepts a seed.

## Tests

New `tests/benchmark/test_gpqa_determinism.py` (no network, no model):

- `test_record_to_sample_is_deterministic_across_calls` — reseeds the global RNG
  between calls and asserts the target letter and option order do not drift.
- `test_target_still_points_at_the_correct_answer` — the letter still indexes the
  correct option.
- `test_shuffle_still_varies_between_questions` — shuffling is still applied
  across questions.

Verification:

- Red→green confirmed: on the previous code the first test fails with the target
  drifting across `{'A', 'C', 'D'}` for a single question, matching the report.
- End to end: `mock_llm` on `gpqa_diamond --limit 8` scored 12.5%, and
  `--use-cache <dir> --rerun-review` reproduced 12.5% exactly.
- `make lint` passes.

## Known limitation

Predictions cached by earlier versions cannot be recovered: the original option
order was never persisted, so a rerun-review over old caches still mismatches.
Those runs need a fresh generation pass. Persisting the target inside the cached
`ModelResult` would make old caches self-describing, but that changes the cache
schema and is left out of this fix.

Closes #1579

title: fix(acebench): align with the official protocol and fix milestone scoring
body:
Closes #1538

Rewrites the ACEBench adapter to follow the official protocol, and validates it
against the upstream repository rather than against our own reading of it.

## Why

The previous implementation approximated ACEBench: hand-written English system
prompts, a lenient call parser, and no rollout at all for the `agent`
categories (it asked the model to emit a final-state JSON blob and graded
that). Reported numbers were not comparable to the official leaderboard.

#1538 is one visible symptom: `score_milestones` returned `1.0` when
milestones existed but failed to parse, so an unscorable sample looked
identical to a perfect one.

## What changed

**Official protocol.** Prompts, output contract, decoding and scoring now
follow upstream. An answer that cannot be decoded scores zero instead of being
rescued by lenient parsing. `normal_multi_turn_*` is scored per dialogue (every
step must be correct). `agent` categories run a real rollout against the
simulated phone / food-delivery / travel APIs and are graded on the resulting
environment state.

**Milestone scoring (#1538).** `milestone_accuracy` compares milestones as raw
strings and always divides by the declared milestone count, so a milestone that
cannot be matched lowers the score instead of disappearing from the
denominator:

```python
milestone_accuracy([], [{'unexpected_schema': 'value'}])   # 1.0 -> 0.0
milestone_accuracy([], ['not a call'])                     # 1.0 -> 0.0
milestone_accuracy([], [])                                 # 1.0 (case (A), left as-is per the issue)
```

**Report.** Adds the official groupings (ATOM, SINGLE_TURN, MULTI_TURN, NORMAL,
SPECIAL, AGENT) and an OVERALL weighted `normal` 0.578 / `special` 0.2676 /
`agent` 0.1545, matching `model_eval/evaluation_helper.py`.

**Safety.** Upstream `eval()`s both reconstructed call strings and argument AST
nodes. Here calls are dispatched with `getattr(instance, name)(**kwargs)` and
arguments resolved with `ast.literal_eval`, so model output is never executed
as code (`test_model_output_is_never_executed` guards this). API instances are
per-rollout instead of module globals, which makes concurrent evaluation safe.

**Vendored code.** The simulated API classes live in
`evalscope/third_party/acebench/{en,zh}/`, byte-identical to upstream, with the
MIT notice reproduced in `evalscope/third_party/acebench/LICENSE`. ACEBench is
not published as a package and the agent categories are graded on the state
these classes reach, so they have to run as-is.

**Observability.** The rollout emits an `AgentTrace` and keeps the model's own
assistant messages, so agent samples render in the dashboard like
AgentLoop-driven benchmarks and `PerfCollector` picks up per-turn latency and
tokens.

## Validation

The scoring logic and the simulated APIs are ports, so the guarantee is a
differential run against the real thing. Point `ACEBENCH_REPO` at a checkout to
enable it:

```bash
ACEBENCH_REPO=/path/to/ACEBench pytest tests/benchmark/test_acebench.py -q
# 62 passed, 0 skipped
```

- `test_checker_matches_upstream[en|zh]` — every verdict on 1000+ perturbations
  per language agrees with upstream `normal_checker`, quirks included
- `test_simulated_apis_match_upstream` — end state matches upstream
  `execute_agent_func_call` field by field
- 22 prompt constants compared verbatim against upstream
- loop structure, execution labels, dispatch semantics, milestone recording and
  policy concatenation checked line by line against `apimodel_inference.py`

Without `ACEBENCH_REPO` those three skip and the remaining 59 run offline (no
network, no live model).

Also run: `make lint`, `pytest tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite`,
and an end-to-end evaluation over all three families with a live model,
including both agent rollout paths and a `use_cache` + `rerun_review` replay.

## Behaviour changes to note in the changelog

- `end_state_acc` is gone from `metric_list`; decoding is stricter. ACEBench
  numbers from before this change are **not comparable**.
- `agent_multi_turn` needs a user simulator (`extra_params.user_model`, the
  official runner uses `gpt-4o`). Without one those rollouts fail and score
  zero, which drags the AGENT group down — configure it before reading OVERALL.
- `extra_params.is_fc_model` was removed. It attached tool schemas while the
  system prompt still demanded a textual `[ApiName(...)]` list, so a compliant
  model scored zero, and the `special`/`agent` paths ignored it entirely.

## Known deviations from upstream

Both are deliberate and documented at the call site:

- **Unknown API.** Upstream leaves `func_call_result` bound from the previous
  iteration and silently reuses the previous observation (or raises `NameError`
  on the first call). We report `Error during execution: name '<api>' is not
  defined` instead. Only reachable when the model calls a non-existent API.
- **`eval()`-only AST nodes.** `BinOp` / `Lambda` / `Subscript` arguments are
  resolved with `literal_eval` and fall back to source text. No ACEBench sample
  carries such an argument.

`agent_multi_step` deliberately keeps upstream's transcript behaviour: only
`user` and `execution` lines are folded in, so the agent never sees its own
previous messages (`get_inference_message` is called solely in the agent branch
of `multi_step_inference`). A model that needs that history will repeat one call
until the step budget runs out. That costs real accuracy but is what the
official numbers measure, so widening it would inflate scores above the
leaderboard. `test_multi_step_transcript_hides_the_agents_own_turns` locks it.

## Out of scope

The dashboard's model-level summary sums `Metric.num` across all subsets,
including the derived groups appended by `_on_generate_report_end`, so a
29-sample run displays `Num=98`. `bfcl_v3`, `bfcl_v4`, `poly_math`,
`needle_haystack`, `gdpval`, `ocr_bench_v2` and `general_arena` use the same
pattern and are affected identically. Worth a separate issue at the framework
level rather than a per-benchmark workaround.

title: fix(gpqa): remove bracket-stripping regex that corrupts answer choices
body:
## Problem

The `preprocess()` function in GPQA adapter was copied from HellaSwag and applied `re.sub('\\[.*?\\]', '', text)` to all answer choices. This strips any bracket-enclosed content, destroying valid mathematical/scientific notation in GPQA answers (e.g. `ln(2) = [ (T_1 - T_2) / (T1*T2)]` becomes `ln(2) =`), leading to random evaluation results.

## Root Cause

The preprocessing logic (`[title]` replacement + generic bracket removal + space collapsing) is designed for HellaSwag's Wikipedia-sourced data. GPQA is a graduate-level science Q&A benchmark with no `[title]` markers — the regex has no legitimate purpose here.

## Fix

Remove the bracket-stripping regex and related cleaning logic entirely, keeping only `strip()`. This aligns with EleutherAI's lm-evaluation-harness which also removed this regex in v2.2 (EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness#3691).

Closes #1446

title: feat(plawbench): add PLawBench rubric-based legal practice benchmark
body:
## Summary

Adds **PLawBench**, a rubric-based benchmark for evaluating LLMs on real-world Chinese legal practice ([upstream repo](https://github.com/skylenage/PLawbench)). Every item carries a rubric annotated by legal experts, and grading is performed by an LLM judge against that rubric rather than against a reference answer.

Data is republished as [`evalscope/PLawBench`](https://modelscope.cn/datasets/evalscope/PLawBench) with **one ModelScope config per task**, so each task is a real subset rather than a client-side split.

## Subsets

The four subsets map one-to-one onto the leaf columns of the upstream leaderboard:

| Subset | N | Official column |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `legal_consultation` | 18 | Task1 |
| `case_analysis` | 250 | Task2-Avg, plus `conclusion_acc` / `fact_acc` / `reasoning_acc` / `law_acc` → Task2-Conclusion / Facts / Reasoning / Statute |
| `plaintiff_statement` | 6 | Task3-Plaintiff |
| `defendant_statement` | 6 | Task3-Defendant |

The three tasks use **different judge protocols** (different system prompts, different verdict schemas; only the consultation judge takes a question budget), so they are not a cosmetic split. Plaintiff and defendant are kept separate because the upstream leaderboard reports them as separate columns.

## Deviations from the official script

All are documented in the benchmark description:

- **Rubric denominators come from the dataset**, not the judge output, and awarded points are clamped to `[0, max_points]`. A judge that mis-reports the denominator therefore cannot distort the score.
- **The `case_analysis` judge template is repaired.** The official one ships malformed JSON (missing comma before `"others"`) and pins the conclusion section to `"total_points": 0`.
- **Judge verdicts are parsed with a string-aware brace matcher plus a repair pass** that closes unterminated strings/arrays/objects. This is needed in practice: real judge output was observed leaving the `suggestions` array unclosed, which would otherwise discard a sample whose `score_details` was complete and valid. The official script relies on `json_repair`, which is not a declared EvalScope dependency, so the repair is self-contained.

Task prompts and judge prompts are otherwise ported from the official release and verified byte-identical (modulo trailing whitespace stripped by the pre-commit hook).

## Reporting caveat

`OVERALL` is a per-sample mean, so `case_analysis` dominates it (250 of 280 samples). The paper's `Overall` column is an **equal-weighted mean of the three task scores** — fitted across the 24 models in the official ranking, equal-task weighting gives mean absolute error 0.72 versus 2.87 for a sample-weighted mean. The description tells users to compare per-subset scores instead. Per-subset scores are directly comparable to the paper.

## Verification

Real-API run across **all four subsets** (`qwen-plus` evaluated, `qwen3-max` as judge, `limit=6` — 100% of both drafting subsets):

| Subset | Num | mean_acc |
| --- | --- | --- |
| case_analysis | 6 | 0.8199 |
| legal_consultation | 6 | 0.8961 |
| plaintiff_statement | 6/6 | 0.5208 |
| defendant_statement | 6/6 | 0.8157 |
| **OVERALL** | 24 | **0.7631** |

- **Scores independently re-derived**: all 24 samples re-computed from the stored raw judge responses by a separate reimplementation using a *different* JSON parser (`json_repair`) — `mismatches=0`, `judge_failed=0`. Subset means and `OVERALL` also hand-checked.
- **Sanity signal**: the per-dimension ordering reproduces the published leaderboard, where `Facts` is the highest and `Statute` the lowest column for every model (here fact 0.989 > reasoning 0.789 > law 0.764 ≈ conclusion 0.700).
- **Dashboard verified end to end**: all 4 subsets render, the heterogeneous metric layout (5 metrics on `case_analysis`, 1 on the others) renders without blank cells or broken tables, radar chart draws, Chinese legal text and the rubric breakdown render readably, no JS console errors.
- `make lint` clean. Tests are end-to-end only, in `tests/benchmark/test_eval.py`: `test_plawbench_mock` (mock model + mock judge, no network) and `test_plawbench` (real API). `tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite` also passes.

## Notes for reviewers

- Requires an LLM judge (`judge_strategy='llm'` or `'auto'`); `'rule'` raises a clear error.
- The drafting subsets ask for a 2,500–3,000 character document, so the **evaluated model** needs a generous `max_tokens` — a truncated filing is graded as incomplete and scores near zero for reasons unrelated to legal ability. This is called out in the description; it was observed in the verification run.
- `case_analysis` and `legal_consultation` are sampled, not exhaustively evaluated (a full 280-sample run is roughly 2h of judge calls).
- LLM judges are not bit-deterministic even at `temperature=0`; the drafting subsets moved by ~0.04 between two scoring passes over identical predictions.

title: feat(screenspot_pro): add ScreenSpot-Pro GUI grounding benchmark
body:
## Summary

Integrates [ScreenSpot-Pro](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07981) (`lmms-lab/ScreenSpot-Pro`) — a GUI grounding benchmark of 1,581 expert-annotated instructions over authentic high-resolution professional desktop screenshots (up to 6016x3384). Given an instruction, the model must output a click point locating the target UI element.

Implemented as a `VisionLanguageAdapter` reusing the standard dataset flow; no new framework mechanisms.

## Design

- **Subsets**: `reformat_subset` groups samples by the record's `group` field into the 6 paper-standard domains (`CAD`, `Creative`, `Dev`, `OS`, `Office`, `Scientific`). Counts sum to exactly 1,581 — no samples dropped.
- **Metrics**: `acc` plus `text_acc` / `icon_acc`. The `ui_type`-specific key is emitted only for applicable samples, so the stock `Mean` aggregator averages each over its own population — reproducing the reference implementation's three metrics without a custom aggregator.
- **Scoring**: strict point-in-bbox against ground truth normalized by `img_size`, matching the official protocol. The effective tolerance is the target element itself (median 57x25 px; icons 26x24 px).

## Two correctness issues found while validating

The first real-API run scored **0.0**. Both causes were genuine defects also present in the lmms-eval reference approach:

1. **First-match parsing.** The prompt states the `[0, 1]` range, so responses that restate the prompt or reason step by step had `[0, 1]` extracted as their answer. Parsing now anchors on the **last** match of each pattern.
2. **Coordinate convention.** `qwen3-vl-plus` answers on a **0–1000 grid**, not in pixels (`805/0.8056 ≈ 999` against ground truth). Normalizing by image size scored **0.0** where the thousandths reading scored **0.5625** on the identical predictions.

Coordinate handling is therefore explicit via a `coordinate_space` extra_param (`auto` / `normalized` / `thousandths` / `pixel`). `auto` infers by magnitude; the 1–1000 window is inherently ambiguous, so the convention can be pinned rather than silently guessed. Pixel-space answers are normalized against the size of the image *actually sent*, since `max_image_bytes` may downscale it (verified: 2880x1800 -> 2592x1620 at `300kb`).

## Verification

- **All 6 subsets** evaluated with `qwen3-vl-plus`, 10 samples each (60 total): overall **acc 0.5**; CAD 0.8, Creative 0.6, Dev 0.3, OS 0.4, Office 0.6, Scientific 0.3. text 0.867 >> icon 0.133 avg, matching the published difficulty profile.
- **All 60 stored scores re-derived independently** from raw predictions — every one matched, including the `ui_type` metric split. 0 unparseable predictions, 0 points out of range after mapping.
- **Dashboard rendering** confirmed via `evalscope service`: overall score, all 6 subsets, all 3 metrics, and per-sample drill-down with the base64 PNG screenshot rendering correctly. No console errors.
- `pytest tests/benchmark/test_vlm.py::TestVLMBenchmark::test_screenspot_pro_mock` and `tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite` pass; `make lint` clean.

## Notes

- `eval_split='train'`: the ModelScope repo exposes only a `train` split (loading `test` fails).
- Docs generated via `make docs-pipeline BENCHMARK="screenspot_pro" FORCE=1`.
- Scoring precision: `extract_answer` formats the point to 4 decimals and `match_score` re-parses that string, so comparison precision is 1e-4 (~0.29 px on a 2880-wide image). Negligible against >=10 px targets, but noting it since a point within ~0.15 px of a box edge could in principle flip.

title: feat(perf): long-context prefix injection via prefix_file/prefix_role
body:
# feat(perf): long-context prefix injection via `prefix_file` / `prefix_role`

Closes #1524

## What

Benchmarking 128K/256K-scale long contexts with **real text** was previously impossible: `random` gives fixed lengths but high-entropy meaningless tokens (prefix-cache hit rate / MTP acceptance rate unrealistic), while real instruction datasets are mostly 4K-8K tokens, so a 128K `target_input_len` filters everything out.

This PR adds prefix injection to the perf dataset pipeline: point `prefix_file` at a long text corpus, and the framework slices it to exactly `target_input_len − prompt_len` tokens, prepending it to each short prompt as a `system` (default) or `user` message — every request hits the target length while keeping real-language entropy.

```bash
evalscope perf \
  --dataset openqa \
  --tokenizer-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --dataset-args '{"target_input_len": 8192, "prefix_file": "long_text.txt", "prefix_role": "system"}' \
  ...
```

## Key changes

**Feature (`evalscope/perf/plugin/datasets/`)**
- `dataset_args.py`: `TextLengthArgs` gains `prefix_file` / `prefix_role` with cross-field validation (`prefix_file` requires `target_input_len`; unknown keys still fail fast).
- `base.py`: load + encode the corpus once at construction (auto-tile with a warning when shorter than the budget), compute the per-prompt token budget, inject into messages; plain-text concatenation fallback for `/v1/completions` (no chat template) with a warning.
- `utils.py`: extract `converge_to_token_len()` as the shared decode→re-encode convergence skeleton; `gen_prompt_decode_to_target_len` (random dataset) and the new `fit_prefix_to_budget` are now thin wrappers that only differ in their `fill` strategy (random vocab sampling vs. sequential corpus continuation). Removes the previously duplicated retry loop.
- Enabled for `openqa` / `longalpaca` / `line_by_line` / single-turn ShareGPT (net −16 lines in the four plugins).

**Tests (`tests/perf/test_prefix_injection.py`)**

## What's new

**1. Typed per-dataset args framework**
- Each dataset plugin declares an `args_schema` (Pydantic, `extra='forbid'`). `--dataset-args` (JSON) is validated against the selected dataset's schema **at plugin construction** — unknown keys fail fast.
- New module `evalscope/perf/plugin/datasets/dataset_args.py`: `BaseDatasetArgs` / `TextLengthArgs` / `TextDatasetArgs` / `MultiTurnDatasetArgs`.

**2. Fixed-length input for real datasets (#1483)**
- `--dataset-args '{"target_input_len": N, "input_len_mode": "cap"|"drop"}'` actively truncates real-text prompts to an exact token length (requires `--tokenizer-path`).
- `cap` (default): truncate over-length, keep shorter as-is. `drop`: truncate over-length, drop shorter ones (every prompt exactly `N`).
- Applies to `openqa` / `longalpaca` / `line_by_line` / single-turn ShareGPT. Truncation primitive is shared in `datasets/utils.py` (also reused by `swe_smith`).
- This is distinct from `--max/min-prompt-length` (which only **filters**, never mutates); `min==max` filtering cannot produce fixed-length inputs from real data.

**3. Backward compatibility**
- `--multi-turn-args` is deprecated and automatically folded into `--dataset-args` (on key conflict, `--dataset-args` wins; `num_workers` still promoted to top-level `--num-workers`). Existing scripts keep working.

**4. Architecture**
- The config layer (`Arguments`) holds `dataset_args` as a raw dict only and has **no dependency on the plugin layer** — the plugin resolves it via its own `args_schema`, eliminating the import cycle (no scattered lazy imports).

## Scope notes
- `input_len_mode` intentionally supports only `cap`/`drop` (no padding — padding real prompts with synthetic tokens would defeat the realism the feature is for).
- Output-side `ignore_eos` was already supported via `--extra-args '{"ignore_eos": true}'`; not re-added.
- `#1489` (workload_trace) is out of scope; the framework leaves an `args_schema` extension point for it.

## Testing
- Unit: `tests/perf/test_dataset_args.py` (schema selection, fail-fast validation, `--multi-turn-args` folding), `tests/perf/test_target_input_len.py` (cap/drop, tokenizer requirement).
- Regression: existing perf tests (`test_request_generation.py`, `test_line_by_line_body.py`) pass; CI smoke `test_ci_lite` passes.
- e2e (real): `longalpaca` + Qwen2.5 tokenizer truncated to exactly 512 tokens; `swe_smith` live construction from ModelScope; **real API** run against DashScope `qwen-turbo` confirmed server-side Input Tokens ≈ 524 (512 + chat-template overhead) with 100% success.

## Docs
- Updated `docs/{zh,en}/user_guides/stress_test/parameters.md` and `multi_turn.md`.

- The adapter uses EvalScope's native `AgentLoopAdapter` and does not depend on MCP-Atlas `mcp_eval`.
- Dataset loading defaults to ModelScope and supports `extra_params.local_path` for local CSV/JSONL validation.
- MCP server transport failures are short-circuited per sample so one failing backing server does not repeatedly stall the same sample.
- `GTFA_CLAIMS` parsing handles the public dataset's Python-list string format as well as JSON-shaped claims.

title: feat(cc_ocr_v2): add CC-OCR-V2 real-world document OCR benchmark
body:
## Summary

Adds **CC-OCR-V2** ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03903), [`evalscope/CC-OCR-V2`](https://modelscope.cn/datasets/evalscope/CC-OCR-V2/summary)) as a native VLM benchmark: 7,093 hard real-world document-processing samples across 5 OCR tracks and 16 sub-tasks, each track scored with its own official metric.

```bash
pip install 'evalscope[cc_ocr_v2]'
evalscope eval --model qwen-vl-plus --datasets cc_ocr_v2 --limit 5
```

| Track | Sub-tasks | Official metric |
|---|---|---|
| recognition | multi_lingual (32 langs), natural_scene | token-level F1 |
| parsing | complex_table, general_documents, formula, molecular, info_board | TEDS / edit similarity |
| grounding | text_grounding, object_grounding | IoU (Hungarian-matched for multi-box) |
| extraction | business_transactions, public_services, regulated_records | field-level F1 |
| qa | blueprint, dashboards_fact, dashboards_numeric, financial_documents | substring match + ANLS fallback |

## Design notes

- **Standard dataset flow.** The dataset is a file tree of `question/answer/images` folders, not a tabular split, so `load()` scans a snapshot and feeds `build_dataset_dict_from_record_map()` — shuffle / `limit` / `repeats` / indexing all keep working. No custom loader, no new registry.
- **Partial download.** `allow_file_pattern` is derived from the selected `subset_list`; the full benchmark is ~5 GB of images, so restricting subsets keeps the download proportional.
- **Local image paths, not base64.** The model layer converts them lazily via `file_as_data_uri`, and the dashboard resolves them through its existing `/api/v1/reports/media/file` proxy. Encoding 7k document images up front would hold several GB in memory.
- **16 sub-tasks as subsets, 5 tracks via `category_map`.** Level-3 scenario names collide across sub-tasks (e.g. `multi_scene_ocr_document_text_SIBR_351` appears under both grounding sub-tasks), so they live in metadata and only drive scenario-specific scoring rules. The report shows the per-track micro average plus the macro-over-sub-tasks number the paper uses.
- **Reuse.** Table scoring imports the existing `ocr_bench_v2.TEDS_metric.TEDS` rather than vendoring a third copy; edit distance goes through `evalscope.metrics.utils.functions.levenshtein_distance`.
- **Deliberately not reused:** the registered `anls` metric. Its normalization differs (collapses whitespace, divides by un-normalized lengths, thresholds after `min` over answers) while CC-OCR uses short-answer substring match + long-answer ANLS with an extra Chinese space-stripping rule. Reusing it would diverge from the official evaluator.

## Verification

Scoring was cross-checked against the official `src/evaluate_*.py` scripts:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 312 synthetic cases (exact GT / char-dropped / empty / garbage / 3 fence styles / trailing chatter), all 5 tracks and all 5 parsing modes | **0 mismatches** |
| 71 real-API predictions (`qwen-vl-plus`), **all 16 subsets** | **0 mismatches, 0 unparseable** |
| All 7,093 ground-truth files parsed | ✅ |
| Multi-page samples (2- and 3-page documents) end-to-end via `local_path` | pages sent in natural order, scores re-derived ✅ |
| Dashboard: `/reports/list`, `/reports/dataframe`, `/reports/predictions`, `/reports/chart` | 16 subsets / 5 categories, values match the report |
| Dashboard media proxy | 32/32 images served as real JPEG/PNG bytes, every subset covered |
| `make lint`, 15 unit tests, mock e2e, `test_ci_lite` | pass |

Two things that came out of the cross-check are worth a reviewer's attention:

1. **Code-fence handling.** The official scorers only unwrap bare and ` ```json ` fences. An earlier revision here also unwrapped ` ```html `/` ```latex `, which silently *inflated* scores, because outside the parsing track those fence tokens are meant to count against the prediction. `strip_code_fence` now mirrors the official regex, and `test_strip_code_fence_only_unwraps_bare_and_json_fences` pins it.
2. **One deliberate deviation from upstream.** The official TEDS tree builder raises `ValueError: invalid literal for int()` on a non-numeric `colspan`, which a garbled table prediction can produce — upstream this aborts the whole run. Here it is caught and scored 0 with a warning (`test_malformed_table_prediction_scores_zero_instead_of_raising`).

## Expected behaviours that look like bugs

- **Grounding scores ≈ 0 for pixel-coordinate models.** The prompts ask for a 0-1000 grid; the official scorer rescales anything above 1.0 as if normalized, so absolute-pixel answers land far from the target. This matches the published leaderboard (`qwen-vl-max-latest` = 3.70 on Grounding) and is documented in the description.
- **7,091 samples loaded, not 7,093.** The dataset repository ships no image for two sample ids (`multi_lingual_recognition/.../0913e4fab7c9`, `general_documents_parsing/.../4a74943cc5a4`, verified against the hub file listing). They are skipped with a warning rather than reaching the model and scoring 0.

## Files

- `evalscope/benchmarks/cc_ocr_v2/{__init__.py,cc_ocr_v2_adapter.py,utils.py,requirements.txt}`
- `tests/benchmark/test_cc_ocr_v2.py` (15 parser/scoring unit tests), `tests/benchmark/test_vlm.py` (real + mock smoke tests)
- `pyproject.toml`: `cc_ocr_v2` extra
- Generated by `make docs-pipeline`: `evalscope/benchmarks/_meta/cc_ocr_v2.json`, `docs/{en,zh}/benchmarks/cc_ocr_v2.md`, `docs/{en,zh}/get_started/supported_dataset/vlm.md`
